title: rootless: fix heap overflow in get_cmd_line_args when /proc/self/cmdline lacks the trailing NUL
body:
Fixes the heap overflow described in #29361.

`get_cmd_line_args()` sizes the argv array from the NUL count in `/proc/self/cmdline`, assuming the file ends with a trailing NUL (which mainline kernels guarantee). Non-mainline kernels (e.g. Android vendor kernels — verified on 4.14.190-perf+) can omit the trailing NUL; then `argc` only counts the separators between arguments, the allocation is one slot too small, and the fill loop (`argv[0]` + one entry per separator + the terminating `NULL`) overflows the array by one pointer. The overflowing NULL lands on the glibc top-chunk `size` field, which later aborts in `sysmalloc` (`malloc.c:2601` assertion) or in `unlink_chunk` ("corrupted size vs. prev_size").

This change counts only the NULs *between* arguments and sizes the array for `argv[0]` plus the terminating `NULL` — exact both with and without a trailing NUL.

Verified locally: on the affected kernel, podman built from this branch runs `pull` and starts containers without any allocator workaround.

- [x] Tests pass? — built and exercised on the affected kernel (pull + container run); no project-wide test suite run (device constraints)
- [x] Documentation — none affected
